slides.heading: The Five Classes of Adverbs
bullets: Adverbs of Time answer “when?”:  now, soon, always, never, then.
Adverbs of Place answer “where?”:  here, there, above, away, near.
Adverbs of Cause answer “why?”:  why, therefore, wherefore.
Adverbs of Manner answer “how?”:  well, badly, slowly, wisely.   ·   Adverbs of Degree answer “how much?”:  very, almost, quite, too.

slides.heading: Practice — Which Class of Adverb?
slides.instruction: Tell the class: time, place, cause, manner, or degree.

slides.heading: Comparison of Adverbs
bullets: Many adverbs compare, just like adjectives.
Short adverbs add -er, -est:  fast, faster, fastest;  soon, sooner, soonest.
Adverbs ending in -ly use more, most:  wisely, more wisely, most wisely.
Some are irregular:  well, better, best;  little, less, least.

slides.heading: Practice — Compare the Adverb
slides.instruction: Give the comparative and the superlative of each adverb.

slides.heading: Classes of Conjunctions
bullets: Coordinate — join elements of equal rank:  and, but, or, nor.
Subordinate — join elements of unequal rank:  if, because, that, when, although.
Correlative — work in pairs:  both…and, either…or, neither…nor, not only…but also.
The kind depends on whether the parts joined are equal or unequal.

slides.heading: Practice — Which Kind of Conjunction?
slides.instruction: Tell whether each is coordinate, subordinate, or correlative.

slides.heading: The Interjection
bullets: An Interjection is a word expressing sudden emotion, thrown into a sentence.
It neither affirms nor denies — it just bursts out.
Almost any word can be an interjection when shouted as an exclamation.
Ex. — Oh!  Ah!  Alas!  Hurrah!  Hush!  Ouch!

slides.heading: Fixing Common Errors
bullets: Say isn’t or aren’t — never ain’t:  “She isn’t here.”
Say might have — never “might of”:  “I might have gone.”
State general truths in the present:  “The earth is round,” not “was round.”
Match the verb to the subject:  “The scissors are dull.”  “Henry and Charles were glad.”

slides.heading: Practice — Fix the Error
slides.instruction: Each sentence has a mistake. Give the correct word(s).

items: Name the five classes of adverbs.
What do adverbs of manner answer?

answers: Time, place, cause, manner, and degree.
A word that expresses sudden emotion.
